short_description: One of the patient's own cytotoxic T cells, engineered in the lab to carry a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR): an antibody-derived recognition head on the outside fused to T-cell-receptor activation domains on the inside, letting the cell recognize a chosen surface marker directly, bypassing MHC presentation. Usually made using a lentiviral vector that writes the CAR gene into the patient's own T cells, expanded in the lab and infused back.

labels.en: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) — extracellular recognition domain (scFv)
CAR — intracellular signalling domains (CD3ζ + co-stimulatory domain)

reference.note: This is the identical public-domain NIAID 'Healthy Human T Cell' plate already used in the atlas as the reference for cytotoxic-t-cell (renders/set/immune-cells). Reused deliberately, not substituted quietly: a CAR-T cell is a genetically modified but morphologically ordinary cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and the chimeric antigen receptor it carries is a surface molecule far below SEM/light-microscopy resolution — no freely-licensed micrograph exists (or could exist) that visually distinguishes a CAR-T cell from an unmodified T cell. Disclosed explicitly in the caption per the chlamydia-felis/feline-immunodeficiency-virus precedent for reporting this kind of gap rather than hiding it.
